extracted.intended_audience: preLighters, preprint curators, researchers and community managers interested in preprint discovery and curation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and platform-oriented criteria for discovering, evaluating, curating, and spotlighting preprints (how platforms and curators should surface and annotate preprints for broader audiences). Focuses on features, trust indicators, and community practices for preprint curation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation of preprint peer review outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Offers a single platform that aggregates (preprint) peer review outputs, allowing researchers to easily access, curate and organise the literature and associated reviews into dedicated lists, all in one place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregation should make discovery and organisation easier and save researchers time by centralising formal reviews, curation statements, and comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple reviews for a single preprint
rubrics_metrics.description: Value and highlight multiple reviews for a single preprint to provide diverse perspectives and a fuller evaluation of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support indexing and surfacing of multiple review objects for the same preprint (example projects: NCRC); multiple evaluations act as trust indicators for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader‑centric assessment statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Highlight reader‑centric statements that provide an assessment or endorsement of a particular preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These short, evaluative statements help users decide whether a preprint merits further reading or scrutiny and function as concise trust/interest signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commenting features for added insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide commenting functionality that lets users add insights on why research merits further reading or scrutiny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments should be able to add context and explanations, enabling community discussion beyond formal reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signals of which expert groups have curated an item
rubrics_metrics.description: Surface which expert evaluating groups have added a particular preprint to their reading lists as a trust indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit signals about which groups endorse or follow a preprint help readers make informed judgements about relevance and authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of evaluation metadata into publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate evaluation metadata (reviews, curator notes, endorsements) into the publication record or into the platform's representation of the preprint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding evaluation metadata increases visibility of assessments and can be combined with recommendation tools to elevate important work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human‑led curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasise the value of human curators: researchers find human‑led curation compelling for surfacing preprints deemed important or interesting by peer groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms should support and showcase curator expertise and their curated selections as complementary to automated signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curator context via list titles, descriptions, and imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow curators to express the reason for curating items by creating multiple lists, editing list titles and descriptions, and (for group reps) adding imagery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit contextual metadata (why items were saved/curated) helps other users understand list purpose (e.g., reading vs highlighting) and increases discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusivity and multilingual support
rubrics_metrics.description: Support collaborations with multilingual partners and represent evaluations from diverse groups to broaden content by language, demographics, and subject areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise partnerships (e.g., SciELO) and representation of non‑English or regionally focused evaluating groups to make curation inclusive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of community evaluation initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent evaluations from community initiatives (e.g., PREreview Clubs) and other grassroots groups on the platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ingest and display club/grassroots evaluations to diversify viewpoints and include emerging evaluator communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for multiple preprint servers/subject areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand platform support beyond life sciences and medicine to other preprint servers (e.g., OSF preprints) to provide a broader range of research resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broader ingestion increases value for users across disciplines and avoids siloing to particular fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: User feedback-driven development
rubrics_metrics.description: Use user interviews, focus groups, and surveys to identify user needs and prioritise product improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iterative development informed by widely and deeply felt problems ensures the platform evolves to meet community needs (example: saved articles list improvements came from feedback).

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated screening and AI recommendation tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ automated screening tools and AI recommendation systems to help triage and surface relevant/salient preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine automated screening with human curation (e.g., NCRC, AI recs) to scale discovery while retaining quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced feed functionality to surface diverse content
rubrics_metrics.description: Surface diverse content in feeds beyond preprints themselves, such as review activity, curator lists, and user engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feeds should prioritise relevant, diverse signals so researchers can rapidly access research and related evaluation activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capture cross‑platform discussions meaningfully
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture and represent discussions about preprints happening across other platforms (e.g., Slack, Twitter) in a meaningful way that builds trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrating cross‑platform signals helps aggregate community conversation and provides additional context for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritise user experience to avoid information overload
rubrics_metrics.description: Design the platform experience so researchers can discover and engage with relevant research without feeling overwhelmed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance surfacing useful signals with UX choices that reduce cognitive load; be responsive to diverse user needs and preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explore diverse media formats to increase accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer different media formats (podcasts, video sessions) to cater to varied preferences in consuming research material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternative media can broaden accessibility and engage audiences who prefer non‑text formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage societies and open publishing initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage broader engagement from society publishers and create networks that highlight benefits of open publishing and new peer review models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnering with societies can help re‑imagine peer review practices and elevate curated work within existing scholarly communities.
